title: Open-subgroup local effacement of positive evaluated norm-algebraic bar rows
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with the extended norm topology, a finite intermediate field $E$, an integer $d\geq0$, a profinite group $G$, and a homomorphism $\rho:G\to\mathrm{GL}_d(E)$ defining a jointly continuous action on $E^d$. Put $A(S)=C(S,\Omega)$ with ALL continuous functions [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and $N=A^d$ with its induced internal $G$-action [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Work on the small coherent profinite site in [def-weil-size-convention], in ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix a nonnegative equivariant injective resolution $N[0]\to I^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For every open subgroup $J\subseteq G$, including $G$, put $D_J^{p,q}=I^q(J^p)$ for $p,q\geq0$, zero otherwise. Its vertical differential $d_v$ is induced by $I$, and its horizontal differential $d_h$ is the action-dependent inhomogeneous alternating bar differential of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. Equivalently its terms are the point evaluations of $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline J^p],UI^q)$. These commuting differentials define a first-quadrant double complex [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Define the vertical cohomology row $V_{J,q}^p=\ker d_v^{p,q}/\operatorname{im}d_v^{p,q-1}$, with horizontal differential induced by $d_h$. Restriction along $J^p\hookrightarrow G^p$ gives $r_J:V_{G,q}^\bullet\to V_{J,q}^\bullet$.

For every $q\geq1$, $p\geq0$, and $x\in V_{G,q}^p$ with $d_hx=0$, there exist an open subgroup $H\subseteq G$ and $y\in V_{H,q}^{p-1}$ such that
$$r_H(x)=d_hy,$$
where $V_{H,q}^{-1}=0$. For $p=0$ this says $r_H(x)=0$. These are actual algebraic cohomology classes, without closure of boundaries. The field $\Omega$ remains incomplete, and there is no assumption that the separate section complexes $I^\bullet(J^p)$ are acyclic in positive degrees. No finite generation or cohomological dimension bound on $G$ is assumed.
